narrative: Mining diversification continues: F2Pool (a top-tier global mining pool operator) added Pearl merged-mining support on July 21, and 6block's Pearl Miner software added multi-pool support (Fortune Pool, f2pool, Lucky Pool, Herominers, Alpha Pool) on July 24 — both now added to the catalog. Difficulty keeps easing (29.3M → 27.5M) but block time actually tightened (402s → 319s), consistent with real hashrate holding steady while difficulty catches down from the post-MoE-fork adjustment, not a health problem. Bridge activity was quiet — zero deposits, a few small burns, custody down a fraction of a percent, all ordinary. Social mentions rose again (255, from 167) driven almost entirely by an escalating wave of templated pump-signal spam; flagged in the summary rather than read as genuine interest.

social.summary: Mentions rose again to 255 (from 167), and the increase is almost entirely an escalating wave of templated pump/breakout-signal spam ("#PRL breakout + Backtest done", "rebuy #Prl here", leveraged LONG signal cards) posted by a growing cluster of accounts — not organic interest. The one substantive thread was mining-related: F2Pool and 6block's Pearl Miner both announced expanded Pearl support this week (see network/ecosystem). Pearlbridge's own account continued its dev-education cadence (no user database, no presale/team allocation, burn() has no admin backdoor). incidents.summary: Pearl's July 1 MoE (mixture-of-experts) PoW extension had an economic-pricing bug: sparse expert-routed proofs were credited as full dense-difficulty work, letting miners claim outsized rewards without proportional real compute (not proof forgery, no PearlBridge custody impact, and DeFiLlama's hack database lists nothing for Pearl). Reported network hashrate rose from ~30 EH/s to 90+ EH/s over three weeks as this was exploited. The core team activated a dense-only PoW fork at mainnet height ~91,630 to shut off MoE crediting, with a same-day hotfix for a template-classification bug in the fork logic itself. Current chain height (91,737) is past the fork — the fix is live.

MinePRL, the canonical community pool tracked by this dashboard, is offline (site redirects visitors to prlscan.com); exact offline date within the past ~6 weeks is unconfirmed. Network hashrate and pool worker-count fields are null this snapshot pending a replacement public data source.
